steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Oxidation = loss of e⁻ (OIL RIG); Oxidation state rules: element=0, Group 1=+1, O=-2 (exc peroxides), H=+1 (exc hydrides)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Half-equations: balance atoms (O with H₂O, H with H⁺), then charge with e⁻

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cell: anode (oxidation) || cathode (reduction); E deg _cell = E deg _red(cathode) - E deg _red(anode)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Feasible if E deg _cell > 0; Equilibrium: E deg _cell = 0.059/n log K at 298K

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Calculate E deg for: Zn | Zn^2⁺ || Cu^2⁺ | Cu. E deg (Zn^2⁺/Zn) = -0.76V, E deg (Cu^2⁺/Cu) = +0.34V. Is reaction spontaneous? --- Solution: E deg _cell = 0.34 - (-0.76) = +1.10 V > 0 -> spontaneous. Zn oxidised (anode), Cu^2⁺ reduced (cathode). Reaction: Zn + Cu^2⁺ -> Zn^2⁺ + Cu

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Balance in acid: MnO₄⁻ + Fe^2⁺ -> Mn^2⁺ + Fe^3⁺ | E deg (Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80V, E deg (Cu^2⁺/Cu) = +0.34V. Which is stronger oxidising agent? | Write Nernst equation for Cu | Cu^2⁺(0.1M) || Ag⁺(0.01M) | Ag
